source_snapshot.criteria: Defines the maximum hotspot temperature to generate a warning condition in the STATUS_TEMPERATURE command.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no "$DUT_USER@$DUT_IP"  "echo ---pmbus_names---; head -n 1 /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/name 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'pmbus|psu|power' || echo no_pmbus_dev; echo ---i2c_buses---; sudo i2cdetect -l 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'smbus|i2c' || echo no_i2c_tools; echo ---reg_MFR_TEMP2_MAX---; sudo i2cget -f -y ${PMBUS_BUS:?set PSU i2c bus} ${PMBUS_ADDR:?set PSU i2c addr} 0xB1 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: enumerate the hwmon PMBus + i2c buses on the DUT so the MFR_TEMP2_MAX register (0x0xB1, max temperature-2 factory limit) can be read; then, once the user supplies the PSU i2c bus+address, read the register with i2cget/i2ctransfer and return the FULL value. Agent returns the PMBus/i2c enumeration + the register value once bus/addr are given.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: requires the PSU to be PMBus-connected and the exact PSU i2c bus/address from the board schematic; reading a raw PMBus register needs i2c-tools on the DUT. State: read-only, but target bus/address must be verified against the board before using i2cget.

original_test_intent: Read the manufacturer-defined maximum hotspot temperature associated with a STATUS_TEMPERATURE warning, preserving which internal hotspot sensor the value represents and how it is encoded.
original_method: Using the project/vendor hotspot-sensor and PMBus mappings, perform the approved read-only MFR_TEMP2_MAX transaction, retain and decode the complete value, compare it with the approved hotspot threshold, repeat for consistency and retain read-only thermal-status context.
manual_activity: No physical heating or human observation is requested. The engineer must identify the hotspot sensor and supply the command/encoding/threshold, after which the read, decode and comparison are automated.
required_inputs: PSU model/firmware, board bus/address ownership and internal hotspot-sensor identity
Vendor MFR_TEMP2_MAX transaction, response width, PEC, numeric encoding, scaling and units
Expected hotspot maximum and comparison tolerance/rule
Approved non-forced reader/version, authenticated access and recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Do not infer that TEMP2 maps to a particular physical hotspot or copy TEMP1 semantics.
Do not assume 0xB1, byte width or temperature format; prohibit `-f`, blind scans and writes.
Do not inject heat, alter thresholds or STATUS_TEMPERATURE, clear logs, reset or change PSU configuration.
Use authenticated transport and stop on target ambiguity, undecodable output or bus/PSU/BMC/host change.
No automatic retry with another mapping, address, width, reset or power cycle.
agent_execution_scope: Verify the hotspot identity, target and transaction against approved documents.
Perform the approved read-only query and retain complete raw response and status.
Decode hotspot temperature with units, repeat unchanged and compare with the approved threshold.
Collect status/log context and prepare evidence without deciding the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Provide the hotspot sensor mapping, response definition and expected threshold.
Approve the read-only path and recovery plan.
Resolve vendor-specific ambiguity and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not suitable as acceptance evidence: 0xB1 and byte semantics are unsourced, forced access may bypass ownership, SSH is insecure, only one hwmon name is inspected, ipmitool is unused and the narrative contains malformed `0x0xB1`.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor/board-approved target-locked non-forced reader and documented hotspot encoding; include authenticated transport and full raw output.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Attended Time 5 and Machine Time 5 remain unchanged; the source supplies no numeric hotspot limit.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind MFR_TEMP2_MAX to the documented internal sensor, run two identical approved reads, decode with the vendor temperature format and compare to the project hotspot threshold.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the identified PSU model/firmware, sensor definition and mapped PMBus path.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record vendor thermal/register-map revision, PSU/BMC firmware and reader version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project-supplied PSU vendor thermal and command documentation; no generic 0xB1 definition is asserted.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds traceable hotspot identity, raw decoding and explicit comparison without adding thermal stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A static maximum-threshold read does not prove the physical hotspot reaches or asserts the warning point.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Hotspot identity, register/encoding, units, expected threshold, target mapping and tool.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Misidentifying TEMP2 can validate the wrong internal sensor even when the numeric decode is correct.

project_override_considerations: A vendor API or BMC bridge is acceptable if it exposes equivalent hotspot identity and raw/decoded value. A project-approved threshold completes only that read plan and cannot be claimed as a thermal warning trip test.
expected_evidence: Vendor command/encoding revision, target map and exact approved read
Two complete raw responses, decoded hotspot temperature and units
Expected threshold/tolerance comparison and read-only STATUS_TEMPERATURE context
Preserved log delta and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row consistently describes a maximum hotspot threshold linked to STATUS_TEMPERATURE. Sensor identity and numeric value are missing inputs, not conflicting requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intent is clear and the absent vendor mapping is a readiness dependency. It does not justify permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reject the unsupported 0xB1 forced byte assumption and its lack of hotspot identity.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain its hotspot-specific gates and no-heat boundary; reclassify to FULLY AUTOMATABLE because all core actions after setup are machine-executable.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Prevents reuse of the inlet-sensor conclusion and limits evidence to the static hotspot threshold.

review_improvement: This review treats hotspot identity as essential provenance, defines the raw-to-temperature evidence chain and avoids falsely expanding a manufacturer limit query into a thermal-event test.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike TEMP1, the decisive ambiguity here is which internal hotspot TEMP2 denotes. That mapping must come from the vendor, but once supplied the test remains a deterministic read/decode/compare workflow, so FULLY AUTOMATABLE is appropriate.
